questions.question: Has AI actually reduced hiring of young workers in AI-exposed occupations?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — employment of workers aged 22-25 in AI-exposed occupations now sits about 19% below where it would be had it kept pace with less-exposed peers.

questions.question: Is AI causing layoffs of junior employees, or something else?
questions.answer_summary: The decline shows up primarily through reduced hiring of young workers rather than through increased separations/layoffs.

questions.question: Do experienced workers in the same AI-exposed occupations show the same decline as young workers?
questions.answer_summary: No — experienced workers in the same roles show no comparable employment decline.

questions.question: Are all AI-exposed jobs affected the same way?
questions.answer_summary: No — the research distinguishes 'substitution' roles (AI replacing tasks), where employment declined, from 'complementary' roles (AI assisting workers), where employment stayed flat or even increased, especially for experienced staff.

questions.question: Does this research prove AI is directly causing the entry-level hiring decline?
questions.answer_summary: The authors are explicit that these are 'early, descriptive indicators — canaries in the coal mine — rather than causal estimates,' i.e. preliminary evidence, not proof.
